paragraphs: The M2 Competition arrived in 2018 as the more powerful successor to the original M2, and its engine choice is what truly separates it from the base car. Early F87-generation cars use the S55 — a 3.0-litre twin-turbo straight-six derived from the F80 M3 and F82 M4, producing 405bhp in Competition form. From 2022, the G87-generation M2 Competition switched to the S58, a newer twin-turbo straight-six that's fundamentally different from the S55 — closed-deck block, revised internals, and a much more robust design that doesn't carry the earlier engine's crank hub concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The M2 Competition is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre twin-turbo straight-six fitted to the M2 Competition from 2018 to 2021 (F87 generation). Known for the press-fit crank hub slipping under hard use, which can throw off engine timing — see the callout above. We upgrade the crank hub assembly as standard on every S55 rebuild, along with replacing the timing chain, bearings and gaskets where worn.

cards.body: The current 3.0-litre twin-turbo straight-six, fitted from 2022 (G87 generation). A genuinely different design from the S55 — closed-deck block, revised internals, and no confirmed crank hub issue. We service it to the same high standard as the S55.

compatibility.intro: Because the M2 Competition spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an S55 part will work on an S58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (S55 or S58) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M2 Competition quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
